answer: Conjuring starts with nothing and ends with a solid object, so the caster has to produce the whole thing rather than reshape something already there. The result is real and usable, not a trick of light. That is why it demands more control than changing an existing object's form.
note: Full answer.

answer: Conjuring produces a real object out of nothing.
note: Correct core, completeness clause omitted entirely.

answer: Conjuring is just an illusion. The caster makes the audience see an object, but nothing real is created.
note: Wrong: calls conjuring an illusion.

answer: Animation gives an object movement and behaviour that suit the role it is playing, so it can act with purpose and follow directions. It does not replace the material: an animated stone chessman is still made of stone. The change is in movement and response, not in biology.
note: Full answer.

answer: Animation gives an object movement and responses so it can act with purpose.
note: Correct core, completeness clause omitted entirely.

answer: Animation gives an object movement and responses so it can act with purpose. The animated chessmen follow instructions.
note: Correct core, omits the material point entirely.

answer: Transfiguration replaces both the material and the shape of the target; it does not merely disguise the surface. The danger is that a result can look convincing without being complete, and a change that only appears right has not actually finished. That gap between appearance and completion is why the subject is treated as complex and dangerous.
note: Full answer.

answer: Transfiguration replaces the material and shape of the target.
note: Correct core, completeness clause omitted entirely.

answer: Transfiguration does not merely cover an object with a new appearance; it replaces both the material and the shape of the target. The danger is that a result can look convincing while still being incomplete, and a change that only appears right has not finished the work. That gap between a convincing appearance and a complete transformation is why the subject is treated as complex and dangerous.
note: Correct but long.

answer: An Animagus changes into one particular animal, not any animal chosen at the time. The form is learned and stays fixed, and the animal is still recognisably the same person. That fixed form is what distinguishes an Animagus from someone using a general shape-change.
note: Full answer.

answer: An Animagus has a fixed animal form that is learned.
note: Correct core, completeness clause omitted entirely.

answer: An Animagus form is fixed and learned, but the caster can switch to a different animal whenever they choose.
note: Correct start, contradictory finish; correctness 3 and completeness 0 under the contradictory rule.

answer: A small object is convenient for checking a transformation. The result can be picked up, compared with what was intended and reversed if necessary; a set of buttons is either correctly shaped with the right holes or it is not. A living target is harder because it moves and behaves, and a damaged wand can ruin the attempt no matter how suitable the target is.
note: Full answer.

answer: A small object is easy to check because it can be handled and reversed.
note: Correct core, completeness clause omitted entirely.

answer: The Vanishing Charm makes an object disappear completely. The caster must focus on the whole object, not just part of it.
note: Off-topic: describes Vanishing instead of inspection.

answer: An accidental transformation can happen when the caster has no settled aim and cannot control the outcome, and the caster may not know how to undo it. Aiming an unpredictable spell at a person or living creature is therefore reckless: the change may be irreversible and the caster cannot foresee the result.
note: Full answer.

answer: An accidental transformation can be uncontrolled and may be irreversible.
note: Correct core, completeness clause omitted entirely.

answer: Becoming an Animagus can fail dangerously, and even skilled casters have spent years learning how to do it. Because the process is risky and the resulting animal could be used to escape notice, the skill is taught slowly and watched closely.

answer: Becoming an Animagus is quick and safe if you know the spell. The Ministry encourages students to try it without supervision.

answer: Concentration is essential because the caster must keep the intended result in mind while the magic takes effect. If attention slips, the target can be left only partly changed, looking altered but never completing the transformation. Knowing the spell alone will not finish it; the caster must sustain the intended result until the change is complete.
note: Full answer.

answer: Concentration matters because the caster has to hold the intended result steadily.
note: Correct core, completeness clause omitted entirely.

answer: Concentration is essential in Transfiguration because the caster has to keep the intended result in mind for as long as the magic is working. If attention slips, the target may be left only partly changed: it can look altered without ever completing the transformation. The caster cannot rely on knowing the spell alone, because the change has to be sustained until it is fully finished, and a distracted attempt may never reach that point.
note: Correct but long.
